state.instructions: Compare these approaches using the stated constraints and code. Do not infer a working runtime from a preferred answer.
state.facts: Availability changes belong to CanRent alone. Each repair captures block_source, block_resource, the time bounds and the manager release evidence. A provider can commit despite an unknown transport result. Provider amendments make equal requests repeatable and report versioned source outcomes through changed. Only location-authorized maintenance_manager recovery is allowed. A pending unknown restoration blocks reopening; old completion evidence survives.
state.actual_code: scenario block(repair:Repair,from:datetime,until:datetime?) by=maintenance_manager; require can_work(actor,repair.parent.location) and repair.parent.resource!=null and repair.state!=fixed and repair.block_state in [none,released] and (until==null or from<until); scenario verify(repair:Repair,evidence:text) by=maintenance_manager; require can_work(actor,repair.parent.location) and repair.state==awaiting_verification and repair.completion!=null and trim(evidence)!=""; RoomsV1.downtime(source:text,resource:text,from:datetime,until:datetime?)->std.OperationOutcome; RoomsV1.restore(source:text,resource:text,evidence:text)->std.OperationOutcome; RoomsV1.changed{value:OperationOutcome}

recovery.instructions: Choose the correlation policy most compatible with recovery after an ambiguous transport outcome.

criteria.frozen: Keep the original business source and frozen target/payload for manager-triggered repeats, bind completion to the active delivery, and process authenticated source updates in revision order. It requires real idempotent owner behavior and gives no assurance of eventual success.
criteria.new_source: Issue another business source on every retry. Attempts remain distinct, yet an earlier uncertain commit can produce multiple blocks whose release ownership is harder to determine.
